text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Michael Wamalwa is re-elected unopposed as chairman of the opposition FORD-Kenya party.
- Armed gangsters raid the residence of an Iraqi diplomat in Nairobi, escaping with more than five million shillings.
- A Canadian company announces a major discovery of titanium-bearing mineral sands on the Kenyan coast.
- Home Affairs and National Heritage Minister William ole Ntimama is asked to quit his cabinet post over disparaging remarks against the government on Saturday.
- FORD-Kenya chairman Michael Wamalwa is nominated as the party's sole presidential candidate for this year's election.
- A taxi driver in the town of Kerugoya undergoes surgery after being hit by a policeman.
- Nicholas Biwott, a minister of state in the office of the president, says he takes great exception to interference by foreigners in Kenya's internal affairs.
- A bill aims to prepare the ground for launching Uganda's National Resistance Movement as a political party if a referendum is in favour of multipartyism.
- A Somali businessman seeks $20 million from the United Nations in rent and compensation for occupation of his compound and premises in Mogadishu by U.S marines in 1993 and 1994.
- Power officials to meet in Dar es Salaam this week on a $122 million project to link drought-ravaged Tanzania to the Zambian national power grid. ($1=54.74 Kenyan shillings)
